findings.text: §67 requires a live promotion's `_index_payload` "under 10 s in total", but its own cited measurement puts four decodes at 52.3 s, so a single shared decode leaves roughly 13 s by that arithmetic, and nothing in the deliverable (opening an existing region) makes one decode cheaper — the section that would `§64` is not declared as a dependency

findings.reason: the gate measures one of the two files the node is told to change, so a node can satisfy it without touching the entry module where a large share of the 22 s start-up sits; retargeting the arm at `import reckon.cli` (or at the verb itself) costs one line.
findings.text: §69's measured arm is `python -X importtime -c 'import reckon.crew_run_commands'`, but the `crew` command's entry point is `reckon.cli:main` (`pyproject.toml:50`) and `reckon/cli.py:403` imports `reckon.crew_run_commands` eagerly at module level, so a lazy-import pass confined to `reckon/cli.py` — a declared write path — moves this metric by zero while the command's actual start-up cost is unchanged

findings.reason: whether the region alone can reach the stated bar depends on the cost of that single walk, which is exactly what §64 is chartered to make constant-time; the plan should either declare the edge or state that the bar accounts for one cold walk.
findings.text: §67 declares no dependency on §64 (its `depends-on` entry is `[]`), yet its Why keeps §64's own finding on the table: `_run_snapshot` stats every `runs/*.json` document to build the index, inside `_indexed_data` at `reckon/ledger.py:1634`, and region reuse removes only the repeats, not the one walk the surviving decode still pays
